questions.question: You deploy a custom container to Azure App Service. The application reads its model deployment name from an environment variable named MODEL_DEPLOYMENT. You must set the value without rebuilding the image. What should you do?

options.text: Add an app setting named MODEL_DEPLOYMENT to the web app
options.why: Correct. App Service injects app settings into the container as environment variables.

options.text: Add an ENV instruction to the Dockerfile
options.why: This requires rebuilding the image.

options.text: Add a tag named MODEL_DEPLOYMENT to the App Service plan
options.why: Resource tags are metadata and are not passed to the container.

options.text: Store the value in the registry as an image label
options.why: Image labels are part of the image and are not read as environment variables.

questions.explanation: App settings are exposed to custom containers as environment variables.

questions.question: A web app runs a custom container that listens on port 8000. App Service reports that the container did not respond to HTTP pings. Which app setting should you configure?

options.text: WEBSITES_PORT with a value of 8000
options.why: Correct. WEBSITES_PORT tells App Service which port the container listens on.

options.text: WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE with a value of 1
options.why: This setting is used for running from a zip package, not for container ports.

options.text: WEBSITES_ENABLE_APP_SERVICE_STORAGE with a value of true
options.why: This setting controls persistent storage, not the port.

options.text: SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT with a value of true
options.why: This setting controls build automation for code deployments.

questions.explanation: Set WEBSITES_PORT when the container listens on a port that App Service does not detect.

questions.question: A containerized web app on App Service must read an API key that is stored in Azure Key Vault. The key must be exposed to the application as an environment variable, and it must not be stored in the app configuration. Which TWO actions should you perform?

options.text: Enable a managed identity for the web app and grant it permission to read secrets in the key vault
options.why: Correct. App Service uses the app's identity to resolve Key Vault references.

options.text: Set the app setting value to @Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=https://kv-rag.vault.azure.net/secrets/api-key/)
options.why: Correct. A Key Vault reference is resolved at run time and exposed as an environment variable.

options.text: Copy the key value into a connection string on the web app
options.why: This stores the secret in the app configuration.

options.text: Add the key to the Dockerfile as a build argument
options.why: This places the secret in the image build process and history.

questions.explanation: Key Vault references, resolved with a managed identity, keep secrets in Key Vault while exposing them as environment variables.

questions.question: A web app pulls its container image from Azure Container Registry. The registry admin account has been disabled. You need the web app to pull images without stored credentials. Which TWO actions should you perform?

options.text: Assign the AcrPull role on the registry to the web app's managed identity
options.why: Correct. AcrPull allows the identity to pull images.

options.text: Configure the web app to use managed identity credentials for the registry pull
options.why: Correct. Setting acrUseManagedIdentityCreds to true makes App Service pull with its managed identity.

options.text: Assign the AcrPush role to the App Service plan
options.why: Plans do not pull images, and AcrPush grants more than pull access.

options.text: Enable anonymous pull on the web app
options.why: Anonymous pull is a registry setting, and it would expose images publicly.

questions.explanation: A managed identity with AcrPull, plus the managed identity pull setting, removes stored registry credentials.

questions.question: A Key Vault reference in an app setting omits the secret version. A new version of the secret is created in Key Vault. What is the behavior of App Service?

options.text: App Service uses the latest version, refreshing the value within 24 hours or when the app configuration changes
options.why: Correct. Versionless references are refreshed periodically and on configuration changes.

options.text: App Service continues to use the original version until the reference is recreated
options.why: This applies only when the reference specifies a version.

options.text: App Service stops the app until an administrator approves the new version
options.why: No approval step exists for Key Vault references.

options.text: App Service deletes the earlier secret versions
options.why: App Service only reads secrets and never deletes them.

questions.explanation: A versionless Key Vault reference resolves to the latest version, with periodic refresh.
